RISK-TARGETED SOURCE TRACE (baseline b77e9fd2 lines 71-106): The runtime derives 'payment required' UI from shift.paymentStatus and awaiting-payment slot flags, using selected slot ID and pendingPaymentSlotIds. UI is only a projection and can become stale after Stripe callbacks; client must refresh based on server state. Test contract: Negative: stale PENDING after webhook or paid-offer failure; positive: exactly matching pending slot and offer appear. This is not a distinct second-reviewer or executed test.

RISK-TARGETED SOURCE TRACE (baseline b77e9fd2 lines 126-173): CommunityShiftsView filters by workspace and selectedPharmacyId, merges fetchCommunityShifts with worker interests/rejections and passes server data to ShiftsBoard. Server scope remains authoritative; client tabs/markers can outlive account changes. Test contract: Negative: account switch and inappropriate internal visibility, rejections under different worker; positive: current worker's eligible shifts and offers only. This is not a distinct second-reviewer or executed test.

RISK-TARGETED SOURCE TRACE (baseline b77e9fd2 lines 40-98): ConfirmedShiftsView derives scopedPharmacyId from activeAdminPharmacyId, but activeAdminPharmacyId is hard-coded null; consequently the client-side pharmacy filter is inactive even for admin personas. This may cause a selected-pharmacy UX mismatch, not proof of backend cross-tenant leakage. Test contract: Negative: admin with two pharmacies selects one, verify only intended shifts visible; positive: permitted multi-pharmacy overview if that's the defined UX. This is not a distinct second-reviewer or executed test.

RISK-TARGETED SOURCE TRACE (baseline b77e9fd2 lines 25-74): HistoryShiftsView similarly sets activeAdminPharmacyId to null and filters returned history only if scopedPharmacyId exists, making local pharmacy scoping ineffective. User-visible scope requires checking product expectations; backend permissions must still isolate tenants. Test contract: Negative: site switch on history; positive: user with multiple assignments sees expected scoped view. This is not a distinct second-reviewer or executed test.
